outcomes.text: Relate the roots of a quadratic, cubic or quartic to its coefficients and evaluate symmetric functions of the roots.
Find unknown coefficients using given facts about the roots.
Use a substitution to build a new equation whose roots are simply related to the roots of the original.
Sketch simple rational functions with numerator and denominator up to degree 2, including oblique asymptotes and the range of values taken.
Show turning points, asymptotes and axis intersections on a sketch.
Relate the graphs of y=f(x), y^2=f(x), y=1/f(x) and y=f(|x|) and use them to solve equations or inequalities.
Use the standard results for the sums of r, r squared and r cubed to find related sums.
Use the method of differences, with partial fractions where needed, to sum a finite series.
Decide from the sum to n terms whether a series converges and find the sum to infinity.
Add, subtract and multiply matrices, including non-square ones, and recognise the zero and identity matrices.
Know singular and non-singular matrices, and find determinants and inverses of 2x2 and 3x3 matrices.
Use and extend the result (AB)^-1 = B^-1 A^-1.
Use 2x2 matrices for rotations, reflections, enlargements, stretches and shears, and relate the transformations of A and its inverse.
Know that AB means B first then A, and link the area scale factor to the determinant.
Find the matrix for a given transformation or sequence of transformations.
Understand invariant points and lines under a matrix transformation and find invariant points and lines through the origin.
Convert between Cartesian and polar coordinates and convert curve equations either way (with r at least 0).
Sketch simple polar curves, showing symmetry, intersections with the initial line, behaviour at the pole and extreme values of r.
Recall the sector area formula half r squared d-theta and use it in simple cases.
Use and convert between the three forms of the equation of a plane.
Recall the magnitude-angle and component forms of the vector product.
Use lines, planes and scalar and vector products to solve distance, angle and intersection problems.
Decide whether a line lies in, is parallel to, or meets a plane, and find the intersection point.
Find the foot of the perpendicular from a point to a plane.
Find the angle between a line and a plane and between two planes.
Find the line of intersection of two planes.
Calculate the shortest distance between two skew lines and find the equation of their common perpendicular.
Prove given results by induction, including series sums, recurrences, matrix powers and divisibility.
Spot a pattern from a few trials, conjecture a result and prove it by induction.
Model a projectile as a particle with constant acceleration and understand the model's limitations.
Use horizontal and vertical equations of motion for velocity, range and greatest height.
Derive and use the Cartesian equation of a trajectory, including cases with unknown speed or angle.
Calculate the moment of a force about a point for coplanar forces.
Treat gravity as one force at the centre of mass and place the centre of mass of uniform bodies by symmetry.
Use given centre of mass positions for a triangular lamina and other simple shapes.
Find the centre of mass of a composite body using an equivalent system of particles.
Use the conditions that forces sum to zero and moments about any point sum to zero, and the converse.
Solve single rigid body equilibrium problems under coplanar forces, including toppling and sliding.
Understand angular speed and use v = r omega.
Know that circular motion at constant speed has acceleration towards the centre, and use r omega squared and v squared over r.
Solve problems of a particle in a horizontal circle at constant speed.
Solve vertical circle problems without energy loss, finding tension or contact force and conditions for complete motion.
Use Hooke's law for strings and springs and understand modulus of elasticity.
Use the formula for elastic potential energy in a string or spring.
Solve problems with elastic strings or springs, using work and energy where needed.

topics.title: 3.5 Linear motion under a variable force

outcomes.text: Set up and solve separable differential equations for linear motion under a variable force, including a = v dv/dx.
Recall Newton's experimental law, the coefficient of restitution with 0 ≤ e ≤ 1, and the terms perfectly elastic and inelastic.
Use conservation of momentum and Newton's law for direct or oblique impacts of smooth spheres, or of a sphere with a fixed surface.
Use a probability density function, including piecewise ones.
Use E(g(X)) as the integral of g(x) f(x) dx.
Link the PDF and CDF and use either for probabilities and percentiles.
Use CDFs to find the CDF and PDF of related variables such as Y = X cubed.
Formulate hypotheses and test a population mean from a small normal sample of unknown variance with a t-test.
Calculate a pooled variance estimate from two samples.
Formulate hypotheses on a difference of means and choose between a 2-sample t-test, paired t-test or normal test.
Find a confidence interval for a mean from a small sample using the t-distribution.
Find a confidence interval for a difference of means using a t or normal distribution.
Fit a theoretical distribution prescribed by a hypothesis to given data.
Carry out a chi-squared goodness of fit test with correct degrees of freedom, combining classes so expected frequencies are at least 5.
Carry out a chi-squared test of independence on a contingency table with correct degrees of freedom.
Understand non-parametric tests and when they are useful.
Understand the basis of the sign test and Wilcoxon signed-rank and rank-sum tests.
Use a single-sample sign test and Wilcoxon signed-rank test for a population median.
Use paired-sample sign, Wilcoxon matched-pairs and rank-sum tests to test whether populations are identical.
Understand the PGF and construct and use it for discrete uniform, binomial, geometric and Poisson distributions.
Use PGF formulae for mean and variance.
Use the fact that the PGF of a sum of independent variables is the product of their PGFs.
Define sinh, cosh, tanh, sech, cosech and coth using the exponential function.
Sketch the graphs of the hyperbolic functions.
Prove and use hyperbolic identities that mirror the trigonometric ones.
Define the inverse hyperbolic functions, derive their logarithmic forms and use them.
Write three linear equations in three unknowns as a matrix equation and vice versa.
Understand consistent and inconsistent systems, link them to singularity, solve consistent ones and interpret them as lines and planes.
Understand characteristic equation, eigenvalue and eigenvector for square matrices.
Find eigenvalues and eigenvectors of 2x2 and 3x3 matrices with real distinct eigenvalues.
Write a matrix as QDQ^-1 and use it, for example to find powers.
Use the fact that a square matrix satisfies its own characteristic equation (Cayley-Hamilton).
Differentiate hyperbolic functions and the inverse functions sin^-1, cos^-1, sinh^-1, cosh^-1 and tanh^-1.
Find the second derivative when y is defined implicitly or parametrically.
Derive and use the first few terms of a Maclaurin series for a function.
Integrate hyperbolic functions and recognise integrals giving inverse trigonometric or hyperbolic forms, using completing the square and substitutions.
Derive and use reduction formulae to evaluate definite integrals.

subtopics.title: Sums and area under a curve

outcomes.text: Approximate area under a curve with rectangles to estimate or bound areas and derive inequalities or limits for sums.
Find arc lengths of curves in Cartesian (including parametric) or polar form.
Find surface areas of revolution about an axis for Cartesian or parametric curves.
Understand de Moivre's theorem for integer exponents as multiplication and division of complex numbers geometrically.
Prove de Moivre's theorem for positive integer exponents, for example by induction.
Use de Moivre's theorem with positive or negative rational exponents.
Express trig ratios of multiple angles in powers of the basic ratios.
Express powers of sine and cosine in terms of multiple angles.
Sum series using de Moivre, including the C+iS method.
Find and use the nth roots of unity.
Find an integrating factor and use it to solve a first order linear differential equation.

subtopics.title: Second order equations with constant coefficients

outcomes.text: Know complementary function and particular integral, and that the general solution is their sum.
Find the complementary function for first or second order linear equations, covering distinct, repeated and complex roots.
Choose and find a particular integral for polynomial, exponential and trigonometric right-hand sides, including finding unknown coefficients.
Use a given substitution to reduce an equation to a linear constant-coefficient or separable form.
Use initial conditions for a particular solution and interpret it in a modelled problem.
